_source: Dukes, Kais. The Quranic Arabic Corpus, version 0.4. Leeds: Language Research Group, University of Leeds, 2009-2017. https://corpus.quran.com/. GNU GPL.
_chronologySource: Egyptian Standard (Cairo 1924) revelation order, four-period classification following the Nöldeke-Bell tradition (Watt, "Bell's Introduction to the Qur'an", 1970).

root-frequencies.description: Every one of the 1,642 roots: raw occurrence count, overall normalized frequency, and per-period count and normalized frequency.
root-frequencies.countingRule: Root occurrence = token count from Leeds morphology (root field non-empty). Normalized frequency = (count / total tokens for the given scope) * 1000, i.e. occurrences per 1,000 tokens.
root-frequencies.verification: totalCount and normalizedFrequencyOverall: Verified (direct computation). Per-period fields: Nuanced (depend on the four-period chronology named in _chronologySource).

association-pairs.description: Root-pair association statistics: the union of every pair appearing in any root's top-25-by-LLR partner list, deduplicated by unordered pair.
association-pairs.countingRule: Co-occurrence counted at the verse level over N = 6,236 verses. Only pairs with at least 5 shared verses were computed by scripts/compute-association-stats.mjs; only the top 25 partners per root (by LLR) are represented here, so this is not the complete set of all pairs meeting the 5-shared-verse threshold.
association-pairs.verification: Verified: direct computation from Leeds morphology, cross-checked against a hand-computed 2x2 table and against data/cooccurrence/*.json's independently computed counts.

fields.name: rootA
fields.description: First root of the pair (Buckwalter).

fields.name: rootASafeKey
fields.description: URL/filename-safe encoding of rootA.

fields.name: rootALatin
fields.description: rootA in Latin transliteration.

fields.name: rootB
fields.description: Second root of the pair (Buckwalter).

fields.name: rootBSafeKey
fields.description: URL/filename-safe encoding of rootB.

fields.name: rootBLatin
fields.description: rootB in Latin transliteration.

fields.name: sharedVerses
fields.description: k11: number of verses in which both roots are attested.

fields.name: pmi
fields.description: Pointwise mutual information: log2((k11*N)/((k11+k12)*(k11+k21))), N=6,236, rounded to 2 decimals.

fields.name: dice
fields.description: Dice coefficient: 2*k11/(2*k11+k12+k21), rounded to 3 decimals.

fields.name: llr
fields.description: Dunning's log-likelihood ratio (G2) over the pair's verse-level 2x2 table, rounded to 2 decimals.

association-extended.description: Four further root-pair association measures (logDice, t-score, log odds ratio with a 95% interval, directional deltaP) for exactly the pairs in association-pairs, in the same order and orientation.
association-extended.countingRule: Same verse-level 2x2 table as association-pairs (N = 6,236 verses; a root occurs in a verse if any token carries it). sharedVerses is k11; versesA and versesB are each root's verse count (the marginals). Same pair set as association-pairs: top 25 partners per root by LLR with at least 5 shared verses, so this is not the complete set of qualifying pairs. Measures disagree about rank order by design; no single measure is presented as correct.
association-extended.verification: Verified: direct computation from published counts by scripts/lib/association-measures.mjs, hand-computed unit test in scripts/association-measures.test.mjs. Which measure to prefer for a given question is method-dependent.

fields.description: Verses in which rootA is attested.

fields.name: versesB
fields.description: Verses in which rootB is attested.

fields.name: logDice
fields.description: 14 + log2(2*k11/(versesA+versesB)), Rychly 2008; at most 14, independent of corpus size. Rounded to 3 decimals.

fields.name: tScore
fields.description: (k11 - E11)/sqrt(k11) where E11 = versesA*versesB/N. Rounded to 2 decimals.

fields.name: logOddsRatio
fields.description: ln((k11+0.5)(k22+0.5)/((k12+0.5)(k21+0.5))), Haldane-Anscombe correction. Rounded to 3 decimals.

fields.name: logOddsRatioLo95
fields.description: Lower end of a Wald 95% interval for logOddsRatio (estimate minus 1.96*sqrt(sum 1/(cell+0.5))). Rounded to 3 decimals.

fields.name: logOddsRatioHi95
fields.description: Upper end of the same interval. Rounded to 3 decimals.

fields.name: deltaP_BgivenA
fields.description: P(rootB in verse | rootA in verse) minus P(rootB | rootA absent). Rounded to 4 decimals. Asymmetric: differs from deltaP_AgivenB.

fields.name: deltaP_AgivenB
fields.description: P(rootA | rootB in verse) minus P(rootA | rootB absent). Rounded to 4 decimals.

surah-distance.description: Jensen-Shannon distance between the root distributions of every pair of surahs (6,441 pairs), with a permutation null so each distance can be read against what chance and surah length alone produce.
surah-distance.countingRule: Rooted Leeds tokens only. distance is the square root of the base-2 Jensen-Shannon divergence of the two surahs' root counts (0 to 1). The null pools both surahs' verses, reassigns verses to the two sides at random with side sizes in verses (not tokens) fixed, and recomputes the distance; 2,000 draws, mulberry32 seed 20261018. permutationP = (1 + draws at least as large as observed) / 2,001, so the smallest possible value is 0.0005. bhQ is Benjamini-Hochberg over all 6,441 pairs. Plug-in Jensen-Shannon distance is biased upward for short surahs, so read excess (distance minus nullMean), not distance alone. lowCount is 1 when either surah has fewer than 100 rooted tokens; those rows are kept and flagged.
surah-distance.verification: Verified: direct computation from Leeds morphology by scripts/compute-surah-distance.mjs, hand-computed unit test in scripts/surah-distance.test.mjs. Which pairs count as 'distant' depends on the null chosen; this one holds verse boundaries fixed.

fields.description: Lower surah number of the pair, 1-114, Cairo order.

fields.name: surahB
fields.description: Higher surah number of the pair.

fields.name: rootedTokensA
fields.description: Tokens of surahA with an annotated root.

fields.name: rootedTokensB
fields.description: Tokens of surahB with an annotated root.

fields.name: distance
fields.description: sqrt of base-2 Jensen-Shannon divergence between the two root distributions; 0 identical, 1 no shared root. Rounded to 4 decimals.

fields.name: nullMean
fields.description: Mean distance over 2,000 draws of the permutation null. Rounded to 4 decimals.

fields.name: excess
fields.description: distance minus nullMean. Rounded to 4 decimals.

fields.name: permutationP
fields.description: One-sided permutation p-value, (1 + draws with null distance >= observed) / 2,001. Rounded to 5 decimals.

fields.name: bhQ
fields.description: Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted q-value over all 6,441 pairs. Rounded to 5 decimals.

fields.name: lowCount
fields.description: 1 when either surah has fewer than 100 rooted tokens.

keyness-period.description: Dunning G2 keyness of every root (1,642) in each of the four revelation periods (6,568 root-period tests), with a permutation p-value that assigns whole surahs to periods at random, and a Benjamini-Hochberg q.
keyness-period.countingRule: G2 is the token-level 2x2 of root-in-period against root-elsewhere, all Leeds tokens as the universe (the statistic of scripts/compute-association-stats.mjs). permutationP = (1 + draws with G2 at least as large as observed) / 100,001 over 100,000 random assignments of the 114 surahs to the four periods with each period's surah count held fixed (mulberry32 seed 20261018), so the smallest possible value is 1e-5. bhQ is Benjamini-Hochberg over all 6,568 tests. direction says whether the root is used more (enriched) or less (depleted) in the period than elsewhere. Roots share surahs, so the tests are strongly dependent: the file's calibration block reports how often relabelled chronologies pass anything.
keyness-period.verification: Verified: direct computation from Leeds morphology by scripts/compute-period-keyness.mjs, hand-checked G2 and an exact-enumeration check of the Monte Carlo p in scripts/keyness.test.mjs. Nuanced: the period assignment is the Noldeke-Bell four-period scheme, one chronology among several; every figure is conditional on it.

association-by-period.description: For every pair in association-pairs, the verse-level log odds ratio with a 95% interval inside each revelation period, and Cochran's Q test of whether the four periods agree on one association.
association-by-period.countingRule: Same pairs as association-pairs. Inside each period the 2x2 uses that period's verse count as N and a root occurs in a verse if any token carries it; a period is left empty when either root has no verse in it. shared_* are joint verse counts and always sum to association-pairs.sharedVerses. Cochran's Q uses inverse-variance weights over the periods compared, heterogeneityP is its chi-square tail with (periodsCompared - 1) degrees of freedom, and heterogeneityBhQ is Benjamini-Hochberg over all pairs. Periods hold 603, 1,401, 2,609 and 1,623 verses, so late-Meccan intervals are narrow and early-Meccan ones wide.
association-by-period.verification: Verified: direct computation from Leeds morphology by scripts/lib/association-by-period.mjs, with a sample of pairs recounted independently from the token files in scripts/association-by-period.test.mjs. Nuanced: the period assignment is the Noldeke-Bell four-period scheme, one chronology among several. A non-significant Q means the data cannot tell the periods apart, not that they are the same.

surah-stats.countingRule: verseCount/tokenCount/distinctRootCount and diversity ratios are read from data/surah-profiles.json (Leeds morphology tally per surah). revelationOrder and period are read from data/chronology.json. formMATTR/formMTLD are length-robust alternatives to the raw formDiversityRatio type-token ratio (scripts/lib/lexical-diversity.mjs), included because raw TTR is mechanically confounded by surah length.
surah-stats.verification: verseCount/tokenCount/distinctRootCount/diversity ratios/nounPct/verbPct: Verified (direct computation). formMATTR/formMTLD: Verified (direct computation; formulas hand-verified against fixed-point fixtures). revelationOrder/period: Nuanced (Cairo 1924 / Nöldeke-Bell chronology, one scheme among several).

formulas.description: Every recurring 3-5 word sequence in the Qur'an (18,408 rows: 6,403 root-view + 12,005 surface-view), with its first occurrence.
formulas.countingRule: A sequence recurs if it appears 2+ times, counted two independent ways: root stream (words reduced to their consonantal root; unrooted particles skipped, so matched words need not be consecutive) and surface stream (diacritic-stripped written form, all words included, always consecutive). Only the first occurrence's location is included here; full occurrence lists are in data/formulas-root.json and data/formulas-surface.json.

centrality.description: Network centrality for all 1,642 roots over the root co-occurrence graph (5,211 edges, built from each root's top-25-by-LLR partners).
centrality.countingRule: Degree, weighted degree (sum of incident LLR weights), betweenness (Brandes' algorithm, unweighted shortest paths), and eigenvector centrality (power iteration on the LLR-weighted adjacency matrix), each with its rank among all 1,642 roots. Method detail in data/centrality/methods.json.
centrality.verification: Nuanced: the four measures rank roots differently by design, and the graph itself is a subset (each root's top-25 partners, not every pair meeting the underlying 5-shared-verse threshold).

rhyme-summary.description: Per-surah roll-up of verse-ending (rhyme) patterns for all 114 surahs.
rhyme-summary.countingRule: Verse-final word per verse, diacritics/tatweel stripped (an orthographic proxy for pausal form, not a phonological transcription). familyCount/dominantKey/dominantShare/shiftCount are over the fine rhyme key (last two letters after collapsing hamza seats). meanRunLength = verseCount / (shiftCount + 1). Full method note and per-verse detail in data/rhyme/{surah}.json.
rhyme-summary.verification: Verified (direct computation from Leeds morphology and the Tanzil Uthmani text).

discursive-pivots.countingRule: A verse qualifies if its first content word is idh or idha (Leeds lemma) and it shares at least one non-stoplisted root with the previous verse. A candidate marker of a discursive turn, not a scholar's identification of one; method note in data/discursive-pivots.json.

structure.description: Mechanically segmented sections for all 114 surahs (TextTiling-derived changepoint detection over lexical cohesion), not a transcribed scholarly outline.
structure.countingRule: Per-verse boundary scores from five weighted signals (rhyme-family change, verse-length discontinuity, lexical-cohesion drop, formula onset, discursive-pivot markers); section count set by a per-surah significance threshold, not a fixed target. 34 of 114 surahs get exactly one section (no boundary cleared the threshold). Full method and per-boundary evidence in data/structure/{surah}.json.
structure.verification: Nuanced: a computed segmentation, not a scholar's reading; never attributed to any named scholar. See docs/maintainer-guide.md on the named-scholar outline policy.

structure-tests.description: Four block-level mirror-symmetry tests (concentric pairing, inclusio, formula bookending, verse-length symmetry) over the computed sections in the structure table, one row per surah.
structure-tests.countingRule: Each test's p-value comes from a block-order permutation null (blocks kept intact, 10,000 seeded shuffles, or exact enumeration when feasible), corrected jointly across all 345 candidates from all four tests via Benjamini-Hochberg (q<0.05). Null for surahs with too few sections for a given test. 0 of 345 candidates reached significance after correction. Full method in data/structure-tests.json.
structure-tests.verification: Nuanced: a null result describes this specific mechanical test over a computed segmentation, not the scholarly literature on ring composition, which this site never asserts an outline from.

theme-surah-density.description: Sparse theme-by-surah matrix: for each surah, the themes whose root-family vocabulary clusters most densely in it.
theme-surah-density.countingRule: perThousand = theme-root tokens per 1,000 surah tokens (Leeds counts, minimum 2 tokens). Each theme lists at most its top 8 surahs by density, so a surah's absence from this table for a given theme means it is not among that theme's densest, not that the vocabulary is absent entirely. Root-to-theme grouping is editorial (see themes.html); the counting is mechanical.
theme-surah-density.verification: Nuanced: perThousand is a direct computation, but which roots belong to which theme is an editorial classification, not a computed fact.

formulaic-density.description: Per-surah mean share of words covered by a recurring 3-5-word phrase (Bannister's oral-formulaic density), tested against a length-matched null, for all 114 surahs.
formulaic-density.countingRule: meanDensity{Root,Surface} = unweighted mean of per-verse density (covered word positions / verse token count) across the surah. p-value: one-sided, 10,000 draws resampling verseCount verses with replacement from the pooled corpus per-verse densities. survivor: true if this candidate is among the 228 (114 surahs x 2 streams) jointly Benjamini-Hochberg corrected at q<0.05. Per-verse detail and method in data/formulaic-density.json.
formulaic-density.verification: Nuanced: the significance test's null (uniform resampling across the whole corpus) does not control for genre or period, only length.

fields.name: meanDensityRoot

fields.name: pValueRoot

fields.name: survivorRoot

dispersion.description: How evenly each of the 1,642 roots is spread across the 114 surahs, weighted by surah token count.
dispersion.countingRule: dp/dpNorm: Gries's Deviation of Proportions (Gries 2008) and its corrected normalization (Lijffijt & Gries 2012). juillandD: Juilland & Chang-Rodriguez (1964), over each surah's per-1,000-token rate; classically assumes comparably-sized parts, which this corpus's 114 surahs are not. adjustedFrequency = totalCount * (1 - dp). Method detail in data/dispersion/methods.json.
dispersion.verification: Nuanced: dp/dpNorm and juillandD are independent formulas that can and do disagree; this site reports both rather than picking one as authoritative.

fields.name: root
fields.description: Buckwalter-transliterated root.

fields.name: safeKey
fields.description: URL/filename-safe encoding of root.

fields.name: rootLatin
fields.description: Root in Latin transliteration with diacritics.

fields.name: totalCount
fields.description: Corpus-wide occurrence count.

fields.name: surahsOccurringIn
fields.description: Count of the 114 surahs the root occurs in at least once.

fields.name: dp
fields.description: Gries's Deviation of Proportions. Range [0, 1 - min part share]. Attains 1 - min part share exactly when all occurrences fall in the corpus's smallest part.

fields.name: dpNorm
fields.description: DP rescaled to [0, 1] via the Lijffijt & Gries (2012) correction. Attains 1 at the same extreme as dp's own maximum.

fields.name: juillandD
fields.description: Juilland's D; 1 = perfectly even. Not clamped, can be negative.

fields.name: adjustedFrequency
fields.description: totalCount * (1 - dp): raw frequency discounted for clumping.

root-surah-counts.description: How often each root occurs in each surah it appears in, as a count and as a rate per 1,000 of that surah's tokens (long format: one row per root per surah).
root-surah-counts.countingRule: Count = tokens in the surah whose Leeds root field equals the root. perThousand = (count / the surah's token count) * 1000, rounded to 3 decimals. Surahs where the root does not occur have no row (a missing row means zero).
root-surah-counts.verification: Verified: direct computation from Leeds morphology; per-root sums equal root-frequencies totalCount, and per-root row counts equal dispersion surahsOccurringIn.

lemma-frequencies.description: Every lemma (dictionary headword) in the corpus: how often it occurs, its part of speech, its root if it has one, how many distinct written forms it takes, and how widely it is spread.
lemma-frequencies.countingRule: Tokens grouped by the Leeds lemma field. 3,307 tokens carry no lemma in the corpus and are not counted. pos lists every part-of-speech tag the lemma carries, most frequent first. formCount counts distinct fully vowelled surface forms (with attached prefixes and suffixes, so one lemma has many). firstVerse is the lemma's first occurrence in mushaf order.
lemma-frequencies.verification: Verified: direct computation from Leeds morphology; row count equals the lemma total on Numbers, and each rooted lemma's count matches data/root-analytics/.

fields.name: root

fields.name: topForm

fields.name: verseCount

fields.name: firstVerse
fields.description: First occurrence, as surah:verse.

verse-durations.description: Every verse with its length in word-units and how long its recitation lasts in each recording the Read page plays, one column per reciter.
verse-durations.countingRule: Duration read from the header of each verse's audio file (cdn.islamic.network, the files /read plays): exact frame count from a Xing/Info or VBRI header when present, otherwise audio bytes x 8 / bitrate. Seconds, rounded to 0.1. tokens = Leeds word-units in the verse, as in verse-lengths. Method and per-reciter header counts in data/recitation/durations.json.
verse-durations.verification: Verified as measurements of those files. Nuanced as analysis: a duration is one recording's performance, not a property of the text, and verse-1 files may include the basmala.

direct-address.description: Every verse containing the believers' vocative ya ayyuha al-ladhina amanu ('O you who believe').
direct-address.countingRule: A verse is listed when its tokens contain the lemmas >ay~uhaA, {l~a*iY and 'aAmana consecutively (scripts/build-rhetorical-features.mjs). Lemma matching, so inflected forms count; a verse is listed once however many times the phrase occurs in it.
direct-address.verification: Verified: direct computation from Leeds morphology. Other vocatives (for example 'O people', 'O Prophet') are not in this table.
